claim: Zarattini, Aziz and Barbon (SFI WP 24-97, 2024): SPY intraday momentum with a time-of-day Noise Area = max/min(open, previous close) x (1 +/- VM x sigma), sigma the mean absolute move from the open over the previous 14 days at the same minute; positions are set only at HH:00 and HH:30, stopped by the current band and the VWAP, flat at the close; with volatility targeting (2%, leverage cap 4) 2007-2024 gave 19.6 percent a year, Sharpe 1.33, 1.8 trades a day; the base opposite-band version gave Sharpe 0.61.
quote: trading is restricted to semi-hourly intervals
limitations: Author-reported, no out-of-sample split; costs only $0.0045 per share; paper itself says the optimum is VM 1.5 and lookback 90, so 14/1 is not an ex-post optimum.
independent_replication: Local H-20260922-07 reproduced 2.2 percent a year and Sharpe 0.30 (persist entries each minute); a third-party automated replication reported 0.41. Not reproduced yet with the half-hourly rule; this iteration does it.
impact_on_spec: Group A rule, parameters (VM 0.5-2, lookback 7/14/28, stop variants, vol target) and the paper cell.

claim: Gao, Han, Li and Zhou (JFE 2018): the first half-hour return of SPY measured from the previous close predicts the last half-hour return (R2 1.6 percent, 2.6 percent with the twelfth half-hour; out-of-sample 1.2 and 1.8 percent), a sign-timing strategy earns 6.67 percent a year at 6.19 percent volatility, Sharpe 1.08, before costs, 1993-2013.
limitations: Gross of costs, sample ends 2013; effect said stronger on volatile and high-volume days.
independent_replication: Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens (JFE 2021) find the same last-30-minute pattern in 60+ futures 1974-2020.
impact_on_spec: Group B predictors (first half-hour with and without overnight, plus the twelfth half-hour) and trading window 15:30-16:00.

claim: Zarattini, Barbon and Aziz (SSRN 4729284): 5-minute opening range breakout traded only on the top 20 stocks by relative volume, stop at 10 percent of ATR14, flat at close, 2016-2023 about 7,000 US stocks: IRR 41.6 percent, Sharpe 2.81 versus 3.2 percent and 0.48 without the relative-volume filter; 0.08R per trade, commission only.
quote: Average PnL per trade 0.08R when relative volume > 100%
limitations: No spread or slippage; stop fills in the original are intrabar at the stop price; author-reported.
independent_replication: QuantConnect research (2016 only, 1,000 liquid stocks) reports Sharpe 2.40; its comments flag stop fills one bar late and a win rate near 17 percent.
impact_on_spec: Group C rule, universe filters and stop sizes.

claim: Baltussen, Da, Lammers and Martens (JFE 2021): in 60+ futures 1974-2020 the return of the last 30 minutes is positively predicted by the return in the rest of the day; linked to gamma hedging of options market makers and leveraged ETFs; out-of-sample R2 up to about 2.9 percent for equity index futures.
quote: Out-of-sample R2 for equity index futures up to about 2.9%
limitations: Futures not ETFs; effect reverts over following days.
impact_on_spec: Mechanism and independent replication for groups A and B; says why leveraged ETFs are in the symbol axis.

claim: Concretum (2026-07-08): plain 5-minute opening range breakout on SPY, 2008-2025, has CAGR 1.0 percent and Sharpe 0.14; with enhancements CAGR 12.1 percent, Sharpe 0.84.
independent_replication: Local H-20260918-02 ETF ORB gave 92.7-92.9 percent placebo percentile (no edge).
impact_on_spec: Prior for group C without the relative-volume filter; why the filter and the cost are the decisive parts.

claim: QuantConnect research: 2016-only backtest of the stocks-in-play opening range breakout on the 1,000 most liquid US equities gives Sharpe 2.396; comments say stop orders fill on the next minute bar in backtests versus near-instantly live, and win rate is about 17 percent.
limitations: One year; fee and slippage model not stated.
impact_on_spec: Third-party fidelity check and the stop-fill semantics variants of group C.

claim: Alpaca orders: bracket orders do not support extended hours; time in force includes opg and cls auction orders; stop orders convert to market orders when triggered.
impact_on_spec: Execution semantics for stops in groups A, C and D and the cls exit for group B.

claim: Alpaca paper trading matches orders against the NBBO, fills quantity is not checked against NBBO size, and partial fills of random size happen 10 percent of the time.
quote: Your order quantity is not checked against the NBBO quantities.
limitations: Page silent on auctions and extended hours.
independent_replication: Local probe 2026-10-06: opg orders expired, cls of 1 SPY filled.
impact_on_spec: Why paper fills are optimistic for size and why 20-40 sessions only test execution.

claim: IEX reached 4.43 percent of US equity volume in July 2026, so IEX minute volume is a sample of about 4 percent.
quote: IEX reached a new all-time high of 4.43%
limitations: Secondary; search summary used for the 8 percent exchange-share figure.
impact_on_spec: IEX versus SIP signal check for the paper feed.
